rows.derivation: Any-order half: F-IX writes FILE STATUS, RECORD KEY, ACCESS MODE, ORGANIZATION, ASSIGN (reverse of the printed order); each clause's effect is displayed: dup WRITE 22 into the FILE STATUS item (RECORD KEY + FILE STATUS honoured), random READ by key and READ NEXT in key order (DYNAMIC, INDEXED), missing key 23; F-SQ puts ASSIGN last and F-RD (printed order, same literal) reads its record back (ASSIGN honoured). SELECT-first half: negative whose entry starts with ASSIGN then SELECT; otherwise valid.
citations: cite.py --check 12.4.5.2 'The SELECT clause shall be specified first in the file control entry. The clauses that follow the SELECT clause may appear in any order.' -> OK §12.4.5.2 1)
rows.notes: Negative .err is the generic parse diagnostic `COBOL0001: unexpected 'ASSIGN'` — acceptable because SR1's first half is a pure clause-order syntax rule. Rejected at 85/2002/2014/2023. Positive also passes at --std 2023.

rows.derivation: a) 85: PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL-R (ALPHABET 'a' 'Z' first, §12.3.7.4 7)2.) is shown active (IF 'aa' < '11' -> Y) but is not a file COLLATING SEQUENCE clause, so prime keys READ NEXT in native code-unit order (DOC-A.1-8): 11 BB ZZ aa (AL-R would give aa ZZ 11 BB); alternate key via START >= SPACES: alt 11<B1<Z1<a1 -> primes aa 11 ZZ BB. b) 2002: PIC N(2) prime+alternate keys, native national = code-unit order B<a<f<é: prime B1 a1 f1 é1; alternate B2<a2<f2<é2 -> a1 é1 B1 f1 (locale/case-folding orders would differ).
